note: THE MISSING FILE. app.js:2794 reads CONTENT.rules.encounters?.[enc.def.type] for winXp/solveXp/etc and nothing has ever defined it, so every encounter has awarded ZERO XP. Keys are enc.def.type — VERIFIED against content: the only three types in the repo are `duel` (15), `puzzle` (2) and `challenge` (2). A `default` block catches any type authored later so this can never silently pay zero again.

howToRead.base: Each type carries BASE awards, tuned for a NOTABLE-band opponent (threat ~30).
howToRead.threatScale: Actual award = base × threatScale(opponent.threat). opponent.threat is a real number in content (26-45 observed).
howToRead.walkAwayIsSpecial: walkAwayXp is NOT a flat value — see walkAway below. Erik: 'you should only get xp that way if you are really outclassed and it's a smart move.'

threatScale.note: Multiplier on the base award, from the opponent's threat vs the player's expected threat for their level. CCODE: playerThreat ≈ the same figure synthesizeOpponentSheet uses for an even match at the player's band.

walkAway.note: ⚠️ ERIK'S CORRECTION, and the reason this is not a flat field. A flat walk-away award does not reward CORRECT disengagement — it rewards disengagement, which is farmable (open encounter, walk away, repeat). Paying on the THREAT GAP makes it a reward for JUDGEMENT, and it cannot be farmed because being genuinely outmatched is not a state a player can cheaply manufacture.

fractions.label: you outclass it — walking away from riffraff is a stroll
even match — a token; you learned a little sizing it up
outclassed by a band — A REAL READ, CORRECTLY ACTED ON
badly outmatched — recognising a fight you cannot win IS the lesson

incapacitated.note: ERIK: 'getting beaten should give you a little xp.' He is right and this overturns my round-1 zero. A zero teaches the player that losing is WORTHLESS TIME, which is false and makes defeat feel like a punishment rather than a beat. You were there, it cost you, and you learned the most expensive lesson available.
incapacitated.formula: incapacitatedXp = winXp(base) × 0.20, threat-scaled like everything else

duel.note: solveXp EXCEEDS winXp deliberately: the catalog spent 292 crafts insisting most problems are not fights. The XP table should say the same thing — ending a duel WITHOUT winning it by force pays best.

puzzle.note: A puzzle's whole point is the solve; winXp is present only because the engine reads it for opponent_fell, which a puzzle can produce if it has a guardian.

challenge.note: Challenges are the Coliseum's shape (blind grid) — completion is the honest outcome and solving is the clever one.
challenge._ccode262:
⛔ THESE TWO WERE LOST IN A SILENT CLOBBER AND IT MADE EVERY CHALLENGE FREE TO GRIND. `resolution.json` authors encounters.challenge with defaultFailureCost {health:3, energy:5, hours:1} and critFailureMultiplier 2. THIS FILE'S challenge block replaced it wholesale at load, and carried only XP — so in the loaded game `challengeStage` read no default at all.
⚠️ THE DAMAGE WAS SPECIFIC AND WELL HIDDEN. `rockslide_crossing` stage 1 authors {energy:4, hours:1} and NO health, plainly relying on the default to supply it; stages 2 and 3 author health explicitly. So the FIRST stage of a challenge — the one a player actually grinds — cost nothing but 4 energy per attempt, forever.
⛔ FOUND BY DRIVING THE ENCOUNTER, NOT BY READING IT. Both files look correct on their own; only the merged result is wrong, and nothing was comparing them.

default.note: ⚠️ SAFETY NET. Any encounter type authored later falls here rather than silently paying zero — which is exactly the failure that made this file necessary. CCODE: app.js should read `rules.encounters[type] || rules.encounters.default`.

designNotes: solveXp > winXp AT EVERY TYPE. This is the single most deliberate choice in the file. 292 crafts insist most problems are not fights; the reward table has to agree or the fiction and the mechanics pull against each other.

walkAway and incapacitated are FORMULAS, not values, because both are about the SITUATION rather than the act — Erik's correction, and it is the difference between rewarding judgement and rewarding a button.

Base values are tuned so a NOTABLE encounter (~30) pays ~30 XP against xpPerLevel's L1 cost of 100 — three even encounters is a level at the bottom of the ladder, which is the right early pace. At the top, threat-scaling plus the level curve does the rest.

⚠️ THE MANIFEST IS THE OTHER HALF. This file does nothing until `rules/encounters.json` is registered in content/packs/core/manifest.json under provides.rules. CCODE: that registration IS the fix — the file alone changes nothing, which is precisely how this bug survived.
